note: ICS 630-01 Annex N (ANNEX N - Tajik_Person-Name_IC_Standard_FLTS (U).pdf), p. 2 (letter table); held source interscript-private-references/ics-630-01/ANNEX N - Tajik_Person-Name_IC_Standard_FLTS (U).pdf. Extraction: annex text layer, every value cell cross-checked against the rendered page image. Two-column table read in document order (left column а..п, right column р..я). The value cell for э prints the Latin letter e; the text layer stores the lookalike Cyrillic е (U+0435) — transcribed from the printed image. General Notes: double digraphs as a single digraph (шш -> sh). Skipped printed rows: е — printed value cell "e, ye¹"; note 1: "Transliterate as ‘ye’ at beginning of words, ‘e’ elsewhere" — the value is position-dependent, un-expressible as a plain row. The map encodes е -> e unconditionally (its word-initial interpretation of the note is not implemented), so a plain-row test would also diverge from the printed semantics. | ъ — printed value cell "<blank>²"; note 2: "Leave out entirely; do not transliterate" — instruction cell, no romanization value. | ц, щ, ь, ы — printed value cells "<see Russian>³"; note 3: "Consult Russian IC standard for this letter" — instruction cells; no Tajik value is printed. (The map carries Ts/Shch/Y values for ц/щ/ы from the Russian standard; not testable against THIS page.) Findings (map-vs-source, map untouched): е: printed note-1 semantics (ye word-initial, e elsewhere) vs map unconditional e — map does not implement the note; row left untested. | ц/щ/ы: map encodes Ts/Shch/Y although the Tajik annex prints no values for them (defers to the Russian IC standard) — map rules exceed this page; rows skipped, map untouched.
